title: There is a terrifying possibility that many people in the church world never truly wrestle with.
paragraphs: There is a terrifying possibility that many people in the church world never truly wrestle with.

A person can speak the name of Jesus…
preach sermons…
quote Scripture…
perform miracles…
even cast out demons…
…and still not actually belong to Christ.
That sentence alone should shake every one of us out of spiritual autopilot.
Because modern Christianity has trained people to confuse visible spiritual activity with genuine intimacy with God.
But Scripture never makes that mistake.
Jesus Himself warned us.

Not atheists.
Not pagans.
Not people outside religion.
Religious people.
People who thought they knew Him.
And what makes this even more sobering is that the warning comes directly in the middle of discussions about miracles, prophecy, and deliverance.
In Matthew 7:22–23, Jesus says:
“Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name cast out demons, and in Your name do many mighty works?’
And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness.’”
The Greek here is devastatingly precise.
The phrase “I never knew you” comes from:

οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς
oudepote egnōn hymas
The word ἔγνων (egnōn) comes from ginōskō — not merely intellectual awareness, but relational knowing.

Deep relational intimacy.
Covenant knowing.
Personal communion.

Jesus is not saying,
“I knew about you once.”

He is saying,
“There was never relationship.”
Never.
Yet these people had real ministry activity.

Notice carefully:
Jesus does not deny that supernatural things happened.
That matters.

He does not say,
“You imagined the miracles.”

He says:
“I never knew you.”
The terrifying issue was not activity.
It was intimacy.
Not power.
Relationship.
Not gifts.
Holiness.
The modern church often celebrates charisma while ignoring character.
But Scripture repeatedly warns that spiritual manifestations alone are not proof of salvation.
Judas Iscariot walked with Jesus physically.
Think about that.

Judas heard the Sermon on the Mount.
Saw blind eyes open.
Watched demons flee.
Handled ministry money.
Traveled with the apostles.
And yet Jesus called him:
“a devil”
— John 6:70
The Greek:
διάβολός (diabolos)
meaning slanderer, adversary, one aligned with the enemy.
Most scholars believe Judas participated in ministry alongside the other disciples when Jesus sent them out to heal the sick and cast out demons in Matthew 10.
There is no indication the other disciples suspected him.

Imagine being so close to the visible work of God…
while remaining inwardly unconverted.
That should destroy all pride.
Because external ministry success can hide internal spiritual death.
Even in Acts 19, there were Jewish exorcists who tried using the name of Jesus mechanically without truly knowing Him.
The sons of Sceva said:
“I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul proclaims.”
— Acts 19:13
The evil spirit answered:
“Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?”
— Acts 19:15
The Greek wording is fascinating.
For Jesus:

γινώσκω (ginōskō)
— intimate recognition.
For Paul:

ἐπίσταμαι (epistamai)
— awareness or acquaintance.
But for them?
Nothing.

No relationship.
No authority.
No covenant standing.
And the demons attacked them violently.
This reveals something critical:
Using the name of Jesus is not the same as belonging to Jesus.
Spiritual authority is not a magic formula.
The kingdom of darkness recognizes authentic authority rooted in submission to Christ.
Some people want the authority of Jesus without the surrender to Jesus.
But heaven never separates the two.
Even Pharaoh’s magicians in Exodus could imitate certain supernatural signs through demonic power.
In Exodus 7:11 we read:

וַיִּקְרָא גַם־פַּרְעֹה לַחֲכָמִים וְלַמְכַשְּׁפִים
Vayiqra gam-Par‘oh laḥakhamim vela-mekhashshefim
Pharaoh called for the wise men and sorcerers.
The Hebrew word:
מְכַשְּׁפִים (mekhashshefim)
refers to occult practitioners, sorcerers, those operating through forbidden spiritual power.
Scripture never denies the existence of counterfeit supernatural manifestations.
Satan imitates.
Paul warned:
“For Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light.”
— 2 Corinthians 11:14
The Greek:

μετασχηματίζεται (metaschēmatizetai)
means to disguise, masquerade, transform outward appearance.
This is why discernment matters so deeply.
Not every spiritual manifestation is evidence of God’s approval.
Even prophecy can occur through corrupted vessels.
In Numbers 22–24, Balaam prophesied accurately while loving money and rebelling against God internally.
That contradiction still exists today.
A person can move in gifting while living in disobedience.
Because gifts are not the same as fruit.
The New Testament consistently places greater emphasis on fruit than gifts.
Jesus said:
“You will know them by their fruits.”
— Matthew 7:16

Not:
“You will know them by their miracles.”
Fruit reveals root.
And the fruit the Spirit produces is not primarily spectacle.
It is:

love,
holiness,
repentance,
obedience,
humility,
purity,
self-control,
faithfulness.
Demons can recognize power.
But only God truly knows those who belong to Him.
Paul told Timothy:
“The Lord knows those who are His.”
— 2 Timothy 2:19
The Greek:

ἔγνω κύριος τοὺς ὄντας αὐτοῦ
egnō kyrios tous ontas autou

Again:
relational knowing.
Not religious performance.
This is why salvation is not measured by public ministry moments.
It is measured by whether a person has truly repented and trusted in Jesus Christ.
Biblical repentance is not emotional guilt.
The Greek word is:
μετάνοια (metanoia)
A transformation of mind resulting in transformed direction.

Not perfection overnight.
But surrender.
Real conversion produces war against sin.
Not peace with it.
And this is where many deceive themselves.
Some people pursue deliverance ministry while never pursuing holiness.
They become fascinated with demons while neglecting communion with Christ.
But the goal of the Gospel is not obsession with darkness.
It is reconciliation with God through Jesus Christ.
The center of Christianity is not demons.
It is the cross.
Jesus did not come merely to display authority over demons.
He came to save sinners.
The deepest evidence that someone knows God is not that demons react to them.

It is that they love Christ,
obey Christ,
repent when convicted,
and continue following Him when nobody is watching.
Because even demons believe certain truths intellectually.
James 2:19 says:
“You believe that God is one; you do well. Even the demons believe—and shudder!”
The Greek:

τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν
ta daimonia pisteuousin kai phrissousin
Demons possess accurate theology about God’s existence.
But they do not love Him.
Saving faith is more than mental agreement.
It is trusting surrender to Jesus Christ as Lord.
This article is not meant to create paranoia in sincere believers.
It is meant to destroy false assurance built on external spirituality.

Some people know church culture…
but not Christ.

Some know ministry language…
but not repentance.

Some know spiritual warfare terminology…
but not holiness.
And some can publicly minister while privately living in rebellion.
But there is mercy even in this warning.
Because Jesus exposes false foundations before eternity exposes them permanently.
The invitation of the Gospel is still open.
Come to Christ honestly.

Not pretending.
Not performing.
Not hiding behind ministry identity.

Come broken.
Come sinful.
Come desperate.
Because salvation was never earned by spiritual performance.
It was purchased by the blood of Jesus Christ.

The same Jesus who warned,
“I never knew you,”
also says:
“Whoever comes to Me I will never cast out.”
— John 6:37
The issue is not whether you have performed miracles.

The issue is:
Do you belong to Him?

Do you know Him?
And does He know you?

Late at night…
when the music stops…
when the church service ends…
when nobody is applauding…
when the phone screen goes dark…
Who are you before God?
That question matters infinitely more than whether demons tremble when you speak.
Because one day every mask will fall.
And only what was truly surrendered to Christ will remain.
If this stirred something deep in you, don’t ignore it.
Some people spend years mastering church behavior while their hearts slowly drift further from God.
Do not settle for religious performance when Jesus is offering real transformation.
